cases.purpose: A migration with five distinct defects behind a green test suite. The auditor must find each by reading the SQL against the previous release's query and the project's conventions.
answerKey: reversibility: migrations/002_task_priority.up.sql has no down file, against the project convention and AC-2.
compatibility: line 1 renames assignee, which the query at baseSha (src/api/queries.ts) selects, so the previous release fails after the migration; the spec's non-goals forbid any rename.
integrity: line 2 adds priority text NOT NULL with no default, which fails on a table with rows; the spec requires existing tasks to be normal, and nothing constrains the three allowed values.
data-loss: line 3 drops legacy_notes, which the spec does not ask for and the previous release still selects.
locking: line 4 creates an index without CONCURRENTLY, blocking writes to tasks for the build; the index is also not required by any criterion.

expect.check: verdicts/database-auditor.json validates against _shared/verdict.schema.json
role == "database-auditor" && stage == "code" && covers.headSha and covers.specSetSha256 equal the run brief's
verdict == "changes"
checks.migrations has a row with file "migrations/002_task_priority.up.sql" and reversible == "no"
a blocking finding has category "reversibility"
a blocking finding with category "compatibility" has location.file == "migrations/002_task_priority.up.sql" and location.line == 1
a blocking finding has location.file == "migrations/002_task_priority.up.sql" and location.line == 2
a blocking finding with category "data-loss" or "compatibility" has location.file == "migrations/002_task_priority.up.sql" and location.line == 3
git status --porcelain in the worktree is empty after the run
Does the rename finding cite the previous release's query in src/api/queries.ts, or the columns it selects, as the thing that breaks?
Does the finding on line 2 say that the statement fails when the table already has rows, and that existing tasks must get the value normal?
Is there a finding on the index at line 4, either that it blocks writes while it builds or that no criterion requires it?
Does the summary or a finding identify the engine as Postgres and the convention of paired up and down files?

cases.pass: All deterministic checks pass, and at least three of the four judge checks are answered yes, including old-code-cited.

cases.purpose: Precision. An additive, reversible migration with a constant default and a constraint added NOT VALID and then validated, in a project whose instructions say the runner commits after every statement, must be approved.

expect.check: verdicts/database-auditor.json validates against _shared/verdict.schema.json
verdict == "approve" && no finding has blocking == true
checks.migrations has a row for "migrations/002_task_priority.up.sql" with reversible == "yes", and a row for "migrations/002_task_priority.down.sql"
no blocking finding has category "locking"
findings has at most 3 entries
git status --porcelain in the worktree is empty after the run
Does the summary or a note show the auditor checked the previous release's query against the new schema and the constant default against existing rows, rather than approving without stated grounds?
Is the verdict free of any demand for batching, concurrent index builds, or other machinery this migration does not need?
Does the summary or a note say where the migration runner commits, citing the project's instructions that each statement commits on its own?

answerKey: The project's AGENTS.md states that the migration runner sends each statement on its own and commits after every statement, with no transaction around a file.

So the lock taken by ADD CONSTRAINT ... NOT VALID is released before VALIDATE CONSTRAINT runs, and the validation scan holds only SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE. Having the two statements in one file is safe here.
A blocking finding that the two statements share a transaction contradicts the stated runner and is a false positive.

cases.purpose: The column is added by editing the create statement of a migration that existed at baseSha. The SQL is valid and the tests pass, but databases that already ran 001 never get the column.
answerKey: migrations/001_create_tasks.up.sql existed at baseSha and was edited (line 13 adds the priority column). A database at migration 001 will not rerun it, so the column never appears there while the new query selects it.
No migration 002 exists, although the spec's plan and AC-2 name 002_task_priority.up.sql and its down file.

expect.check: verdicts/database-auditor.json validates against _shared/verdict.schema.json
verdict == "changes"
a blocking finding has location.file == "migrations/001_create_tasks.up.sql" and category "reversibility", "integrity", or "compatibility"
checks.migrations has a row for "migrations/001_create_tasks.up.sql"
git status --porcelain in the worktree is empty after the run
Does the finding explain that databases which already applied migration 001 will never receive the column, so the change must be a new migration?
Does the verdict connect this to the new list query selecting a column that will not exist on those databases, or to AC-2 being impossible to carry out?

cases.pass: All deterministic checks pass and the why check is answered yes.
